message.content:
### Quick ways to tell if Visual Studio Code is currently running:

| Method | How to do it |
|--------|--------------|
| **Task‑Manager** | Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>TAB</kbd>, then look under “Processes” for *Microsoft VS Code* (`Code.exe`). |
| **PowerShell** | ```powershell\nGet-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\n``` – If nothing shows up, VS Code isn’t running. |
| **CMD / Command Prompt** | ```cmd\ntasklist | findstr /I \"Code.exe\"\n```\nIf no output appears, the editor isn’t alive. |

---

#### Want me to double‑check right now?

If you’re comfortable letting me run a quick command on your Windows box, I can fire off one of those checks automatically. Just let me know which method you’d prefer (or simply say “yes”, and I’ll try the CMD version).

Otherwise, follow the table above—any of those will instantly confirm whether VS Code is still running.
